Let  
\[
c=\sqrt{ab}.
\]
The answer depends only on \(ab\). Define \(c_*>0\) to be the unique positive solution of
\[
c\,K_0\!\left(\frac2c\right)=2K_1\!\left(\frac2c\right),
\]
where \(K_\nu\) is the modified Bessel function of the second kind. Then the origin is almost surely exponentially stable exactly for
\[
\boxed{ab<c_*^2}.
\]

Equivalently,
\[
\boxed{\frac{\sqrt{ab}\,K_0\!\left(2/\sqrt{ab}\right)}
{2K_1\!\left(2/\sqrt{ab}\right)}<1 }.
\]

Here is the derivation.

Write
\[
A_i=-I+B_i.
\]
After the diagonal change of variables that balances the two shears, the growth part becomes
\[
B_1=\begin{pmatrix}0&c\\0&0\end{pmatrix},
\qquad
B_2=\begin{pmatrix}0&0\\c&0\end{pmatrix},
\qquad c=\sqrt{ab}.
\]
Thus the Lyapunov exponent of the original system is the Lyapunov exponent of this shear system minus \(1\).

For the shear system, write \(y=\rho(\cos\theta,\sin\theta)\), with \(\theta\in(0,\pi/2)\). In mode \(1\),
\[
\frac{d}{dt}\log\rho=c\sin\theta\cos\theta,\qquad
\dot\theta=-c\sin^2\theta,
\]
and in mode \(2\),
\[
\frac{d}{dt}\log\rho=c\sin\theta\cos\theta,\qquad
\dot\theta=c\cos^2\theta.
\]
Let \(p_1,p_2\) be the stationary densities of \((\theta,\sigma)\). The stationary transport equations give
\[
-c\sin^2\theta\,p_1+c\cos^2\theta\,p_2=0,
\]
so \(p_2=\tan^2\theta\,p_1\). Solving the remaining equation yields
\[
p_1=C\csc^2\theta\,
\exp\!\left(-\frac{\cot\theta+\tan\theta}{c}\right),
\]
\[
p_2=C\sec^2\theta\,
\exp\!\left(-\frac{\cot\theta+\tan\theta}{c}\right).
\]
Hence the top Lyapunov exponent of the shear system is
\[
\lambda(c)
=
c\int_0^{\pi/2}\sin\theta\cos\theta\,(p_1+p_2)\,d\theta.
\]
With \(u=\tan\theta\), normalization gives
\[
\lambda(c)
=
\frac{c}{2}
\frac{\int_0^\infty u^{-1}e^{-(u+u^{-1})/c}\,du}
{\int_0^\infty e^{-(u+u^{-1})/c}\,du}.
\]
Using
\[
K_\nu(x)=\frac12\int_0^\infty u^{\nu-1}
e^{-\frac{x}{2}(u+u^{-1})}\,du,
\]
this becomes
\[
\lambda(c)=
\frac{cK_0(2/c)}{2K_1(2/c)}.
\]
Therefore the original system has top exponent
\[
\lambda(c)-1.
\]
Almost sure exponential stability is equivalent to \(\lambda(c)<1\), namely
\[
\frac{\sqrt{ab}\,K_0(2/\sqrt{ab})}{2K_1(2/\sqrt{ab})}<1.
\]

Finally, \(\lambda(c)\) is continuous and strictly increasing from \(0\) to \(+\infty\), so the threshold \(c_*\) is unique. Thus the full stability region is exactly
\[
\boxed{\{(a,b)\in(0,\infty)^2:\ ab<c_*^2\}}.
\]
